message.content:
Yes, the original Coca-Cola formula did contain cocaine. Here's the history:

**The Original Formula (1886)**
Coca-Cola was invented in 1886 by Dr. John Stith Pemberton, an Atlanta pharmacist. The original formula contained coca leaf extract, which naturally contained cocaine. At the time, cocaine was legal and commonly used in patent medicines. The name "Coca-Cola" comes from:
- **Coca**: the coca leaf extract
- **Cola**: the kola nut, which provided caffeine

**When It Was Removed**
The cocaine content was gradually reduced over time:
- In **1903**, Coca-Cola switched from using fresh coca leaves to "spent" or de-cocainized coca leaves, which contained only trace amounts of cocaine
- By **1929**, the formula was completely cocaine-free

**Why It Was Removed**
Several factors contributed to the removal:
- Changing public attitudes toward cocaine
- Increasing regulation of drugs
- The drug became associated with racist fears when it gained popularity in Black neighborhoods
- Legal and public relations concerns

**Today**
Modern Coca-Cola still uses coca leaf extract, but it comes from a special DEA-authorized facility (Stepan Company in New Jersey) that removes all cocaine from the leaves before the extract is used. The extracted cocaine is sold for pharmaceutical medical uses.

The Coca-Cola Company officially denies that cocaine was ever an added ingredient, though most independent historical sources confirm that trace amounts were present in early versions due to the coca leaf extract.

Sources:
1. https://oboe.com/learn/the-secret-coca-cola-formula-cf0ias/evolution-of-the-formula-the-secret-coca-cola-formula-1
2. https://www.thetakeout.com/1788713/why-coca-cola-had-cocaine/
3. https://www.avenuesrecovery.com/understanding-addiction/cocaine-and-crack-addiction/was-there-cocaine-in-coca-cola/
4. https://thetraininggyms.com/blog/coca-cola-is-worse-than-cocaine/
